topIssues.title: op-conductor: gracefully recover from interop reorgs
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Problem

When an interop cross-chain validation detects an invalid executing message and triggers a reorg, the EL is rewound to the last common ancestor (potentially hundreds or thousands of blocks behind the tip). After this rewind, op-conductor's health check compares the unsafe head timestamp to wall clock time, finds the sequencer far behind, declares it unhealthy, and calls `admin_stopSequencer`. With sequencing stopped, the unsafe head can never advance, creating a **permanent deadlock** that requires manual intervention (restarting the op-node pod).

This means every interop reorg currently requires manual recovery of the sequencer.

## Mechanism

1. Supernode interop activity detects an invalid executing message at block N
2. The invalid block is replaced with a deposit-only block; supernode reports the corrected safe head
3. Sequencer EL receives the forkchoice update, detects chain divergence at block N, and rewinds from the tip to block N-1
4. The unsafe head is now far behind wall clock (e.g. 1400+ seconds behind after a rewind of ~1500 blocks)
5. Conductor health check fires, sees the stale unsafe head, declares the sequencer unhealthy
6. Conductor calls `admin_stopSequencer` — the sequencer can no longer produce blocks
7. Since blocks can't be produced, the unsafe head never catches up — **circular deadlock**

## Expected Behavior

The conductor should recognize that an EL rewind (reorg) is a transient event and allow the sequencer to recover by continuing to produce blocks from the rewound head. The sequencer will naturally catch up to the tip as it sequences new blocks.

## Possible Solution Direction

The right fix isn't fully determined yet, but one promising direction:

**Conductor queries the consensus layer (via consensus-layer HA) for safe chain state.** The conductor already participates in HA, so it could leverage the consensus layer to access safe head, cross-safe head, and local-safe head information. With this data, the conductor would have enough context to distinguish between:

- A sequencer that is **genuinely stalled** (not making progress, something is wrong)
- A sequencer that is **correctly responding to a local-safe reorg** (unsafe head is behind because the EL was rewound to follow a corrected safe chain)

If the conductor can see that a local-safe reorg occurred — e.g. the safe/local-safe heads moved backwards while the sequencer's state is consistent with that new safe chain — it can determine that the sequencer is actually healthy and should continue sequencing from the rewound head, rather than stopping it.

## Additional Context

This issue was also observed on fresh devnet deployments: if a sequencer's op-node restarts and comes back with `sequencerEnabled=true, sequencerStopped=true`, the conductor won't re-activate it because the unsafe head is behind — the same circular deadlock pattern. The current workaround is manually calling `admin_startSequencer` with the current unsafe head hash.

topIssues.title: op-node: support superroot_atTimestamp for non-interop chains
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
## Context

After the super-roots upgrade, fault dispute games for non-interop chains will reason over super roots rather than output roots. op-challenger and op-dispute-mon already consume super roots through the `superroot_atTimestamp` RPC, but today this method is only served by op-supernode, which is interop-specific infrastructure. Non-interop chains do not run op-supernode — they run op-node. Without an op-node-side implementation, op-challenger and op-dispute-mon cannot operate against non-interop chains once those chains move to super-root games.

## Problem

op-node does not implement `superroot_atTimestamp`. Consumers that depend on it today:

- `op-challenger` — `SuperNodeTraceProvider` in `op-challenger/game/fault/trace/super/` (interface `SuperNodeRootProvider`, single method `SuperRootAtTimestamp(ctx, uint64) → eth.SuperRootAtTimestampResponse`)
- `op-dispute-mon` — `SuperAgreementEnricher` in `op-dispute-mon/mon/extract/super_agreement_enricher.go` (interface `SuperRootProvider`, same method)

Both currently take `--supernode-rpc`. For a non-interop chain there is nothing reasonable to point that at.

## Proposal

Implement `superroot_atTimestamp` on op-node so that:

- A single op-node endpoint can be used as the trace/agreement source for a non-interop chain post-super-roots upgrade.
- The returned `eth.SuperRootAtTimestampResponse` is shaped so existing op-challenger and op-dispute-mon consumers Just Work — i.e. no client-side branching on whether the source is op-node or op-supernode.
- For a single-chain (non-interop) deployment the response degenerates naturally: `ChainIDs` is the one local chain, `OptimisticAtTimestamp` has at most one entry, `CurrentL1` / `CurrentSafeTimestamp` / `CurrentLocalSafeTimestamp` / `CurrentFinalizedTimestamp` come from op-node's existing sync state, and `Data.Super` is built from the local L2 output at the requested timestamp.
- op-challenger's `--supernode-rpc` and op-dispute-mon's `--supernode-rpc` can be pointed at an op-node URL for non-interop chains. (Whether to introduce a separate flag name vs. reusing `--supernode-rpc` is an open question — see below.)

## Open questions

- **Flag/URL plumbing.** Do op-challenger and op-dispute-mon accept op-node URLs under the existing `--supernode-rpc` flag (treating any `superroot_atTimestamp`-speaking endpoint uniformly), or do we add a new flag (e.g. `--rollup-superroot-rpc`)? Reusing the existing flag is simpler; a new flag is more explicit about intent.
- **Namespacing.** op-supernode exposes the method under the `superroot` namespace (`superroot_atTimestamp`). op-node should match that exact method name to keep the client interfaces and existing call sites untouched.
- **Pre-upgrade behavior.** Before the super-roots activation timestamp on a given chain, what should op-node return? Options: error with a clear "not yet active" message, or return `Data: nil` with current sync fields populated (mirroring how op-supernode behaves when there is no block at the requested timestamp).

## Out of scope

- Interop chains — op-supernode remains the source of truth there.
- Any change to the super-root format itself or to `SuperRootAtTimestampResponse`.
- Changes to op-challenger/op-dispute-mon trace logic. This issue is about adding the server side on op-node so the existing client code paths can be reused.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] op-node exposes `superroot_atTimestamp` returning `eth.SuperRootAtTimestampResponse` compatible with existing clients.
- [ ] op-challenger configured against an op-node URL can play super-root games on a non-interop chain (covered by acceptance / e2e tests against a non-interop devstack).
- [ ] op-dispute-mon configured against an op-node URL can monitor super-root games on a non-interop chain.
- [ ] Behavior at and around the super-roots activation boundary is specified and tested.
- [ ] In-repo docs / READMEs reflect that op-node is the source for non-interop chains.

topIssues.title: Follow-mode ELSync sequencer cannot bootstrap a chain from genesis (deadlocks in syncStatusWillStartEL)
topIssues.author: wwared
topIssues.body:
## Summary

A follow-mode op-node sequencer (`SequencerEnabled` + `L2FollowSource`, i.e. `NeedInitialResetEngine`) configured with `--syncmode=execution-layer` cannot bootstrap a chain from genesis. As the chain's sole block producer it has no peer to initial-EL-sync from, so it deadlocks before producing any block and the chain never advances.

## Details

At startup in ELSync, `NewEngineController` sets `syncStatus = syncStatusWillStartEL` purely from config. While in `willStartEL`, `IsEngineInitialELSyncing()` is true, so `SyncStep` backs off and never reaches `TryInitialResetEngineForSequencer`; block building is gated behind the same back-off. The only exit from `willStartEL` is inside `insertUnsafePayload` ("skip EL sync when a finalized block exists"), which needs an incoming **unsafe payload** delivered via P2P gossip. For a sole-producer follow-mode sequencer at genesis, no peer produces a block to gossip, and `followUpstream()` early-returns while `IsEngineInitialELSyncing()` is true — so nothing ever delivers the payload. The chain never starts.

This also blocks a "bootstrap on CLSync, then restart on ELSync" workaround: on restart the controller re-enters `willStartEL` from config (it does not consult the EL's existing finalized head at construction), so an idle established chain re-deadlocks the same way.

## Impact

The devstack light-sequencer interop presets (`NewTwoL2SupernodeLightSequencerInterop`) cannot run on ELSync from genesis. `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` and `TestLightSequencerSupernodeDerivesSafeChain` are affected and have been skipped pending a fix.

## Notes

This looks like the same `willStartEL` deadlock as the (closed) #11016 — "op-node: EL sync mode prevents active sequencer start-up" — where an active sequencer *restarting* under EL sync couldn't resume because it needs an unsafe payload to leave `willStartEL` but cannot produce one until it does. Here it's a follow-mode sequencer at *genesis*, same root cause.

#21120 attempted a fix but is left as a draft and is likely not the right solution.

Related: #21119 (parent), #21125 (follow-mode reorg-recovery flakiness), #11016 (prior closed issue, same mechanism).

topPRs.title: feat(contracts): integrate L2CM into L2 genesis
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

PoC for routing L2 genesis proxy-side predeploy setup through `L2ContractsManager`.

This adds a genesis-only `L2ContractsManager.deploy(FullConfig)` path. `upgrade()` remains the fork-upgrade path through `L2ProxyAdmin`.

Key points:

- No `L2ProxyAdmin` source/interface/semver changes.
- Genesis still owns proxy/code etching, code-namespace implementations, implementation-account lock initialization, preinstalls, feature flags, fork activation setup, prefunds, and deprecated/non-proxied predeploys.
- L2CM now owns the proxy-side upgrade/init/config sequence at genesis.
- Genesis deploys a temporary L2CM, batch-swaps touched proxy admins to it, calls `deploy(config)`, restores admins to `0x18`, then wipes the temporary L2CM.
- Intended as a draft PR to validate the approach before merge review.

**Tests**

Added/updated coverage for:

- L2CM deploy mode and existing upgrade mode
- deploy-mode `L2ContractsManagerUtils` behavior
- L2 genesis script paths: default, CGT, interop, CGT+interop
- op-deployer L2 genesis alloc invariants
- L2 fork-upgrade coverage

Locally run:

```bash
cd packages/contracts-bedrock
mise exec -- just test --match-contract L2ContractsManager
mise exec -- just test --match-path test/scripts/L2Genesis.t.sol
mise exec -- just test --match-path test/L2/L2GenesisForkUpgrade.t.sol
mise exec -- just snapshots-check-no-build
mise exec -- just semver-diff-check-no-build

cd ../../op-deployer
mise exec -- just test './pkg/deployer/integration_test -run TestL2GenesisAllocsInvariants -count=1'
mise exec -- just test './pkg/deployer/integration_test -run ^TestEndToEndBootstrapApply$ -count=1'
```

Known local note: `interfaces-check-no-build` currently fails on unrelated `IZKDisputeGame` interface/artifact mismatches, not on the L2CM interface changes in this branch.

**Additional context**

Issue #20903 asks for L2CM to become the source of truth for L2 genesis predeploy setup without regressing produced L2 allocs.

This PR uses `deploy(FullConfig)` instead of executing the NUT bundle during genesis. The NUT-bundle path changes the alloc shape through CREATE2 implementation addresses and helper execution state. This PoC keeps the current code-namespace implementation layout.

**Metadata**

- Refs ethereum-optimism/optimism#20903

topPRs.title: feat(op-reth/proofs): snapshot hashed-leaf tables for backfill
topPRs.author: dhyaniarun1993
topPRs.body:
**Description**

**Why**
Snapshot-accelerated backfill was still bottlenecked on hashed-leaf reads. The trie snapshot replaced the V2-trie merge walk, but `compute_block_backfill_diff` were still constructing `OpProofsHashedAccountCursorFactory` at `block_number`, which does the full `V2HashedAccounts + History + ChangeSets` merge at each block. With the trie diff dominated by leaf reads under `StateRoot::root_with_updates`, the per-block cost stayed high.

**What**
Extend the snapshot to cache hashed leaves alongside trie nodes, so the snapshot read path for backfill is fully history-merge-free.

**Tests**

- [x] backfill tests covers the change as well.
- [x] op-mainnet test run in progress 

**Additional context**

NA

**Metadata**

NA

topPRs.title: feat(op-chain-ops): add check-interop smoke-test CLI
topPRs.author: jelias2
topPRs.body:
## Overview

Adds a small CLI under `op-chain-ops/cmd/check-interop` for smoke-testing interop cross-chain messaging against a running pair of L2 chains.

## Subcommands

- **`roundtrip`** — bridges ETH `A -> B` and `B -> A` via the `SuperchainETHBridge` predeploy, relaying each message itself through `L2ToL2CrossDomainMessenger.relayMessage` (no autorelayer), and asserts a fresh recipient is credited the exact bridged amount on each destination chain. No contract deploys — it uses the predeploys that already exist on every OP chain.
- **`failsafe`** — verifies the op-interop-filter failsafe lifecycle via the filter admin RPC: a bridge succeeds, its relay is rejected while failsafe is enabled (`admin_setFailsafeEnabled`), and succeeds again once disabled.

## Usage

Flags can be supplied via CLI, `CHECK_INTEROP_*` env vars, or a TOML config file (`--config`, see `config.example.toml`); CLI and env values override the file. Endpoints can be any reachable RPC URL (e.g. a devnet's direct ingress), so no `kubectl port-forward` is required.

```
go run ./op-chain-ops/cmd/check-interop roundtrip \
  --l2-a <chain-A EL RPC> --l2-b <chain-B EL RPC> \
  --account <funded test key, no 0x> --relay-timeout 5m
```

## Testing

- `roundtrip` verified live against the `interop-reorg-0` dev devnet (direct ingress URLs, no port-forward): full `A<->B` round-trip lands in ~20s when the network is healthy, with both legs asserting the recipient gained exactly 0.01 ETH on the destination chain.
- `failsafe` is **not** exercised live in this PR — it requires the op-interop-filter admin RPC + JWT. It compiles and shares the verified `bridgeETH` / `Success.Eval` plumbing, but the enable→block→disable lifecycle has not been run against a live filter.
- `go build`, `go vet`, `gofmt`, and the repo's custom `op-golangci-lint` all pass (0 issues).
